sentences.text: Valeria fixes Nexo's answer about returns.
She selects Publish and goes home happy.
The next morning, Marta from sales opens Teams and asks about returns.
She gets the old answer.
Is Nexo broken?
No.
Today you learn what Publish really does, where your users meet the agent, and why some of them still see yesterday's version.

scenes.title: A new edition of the manual

sentences.text: Think of the agent as a manual.
While you edit, your changes are a draft on your desk.
Publish prints the new edition and hands it out to everyone.
But someone still reading the old edition won't see the changes until they pick up the new one.
And the places where users pick it up are called channels.
Teams, a website, a mobile app.
First rule.
Saving is not publishing.
Your saved changes stay in your draft, and only you see them in the test pane.
When you select Publish, every connected channel is updated at once.
Teams, the website and the mobile app get the same new edition together.
So you never republish channel by channel.
One Publish is enough.
Your turn.
Valeria saved a change, and it works in the test pane.
But users on Teams and on the website don't see it, even in new conversations.
What is missing?
Republish each channel one by one?
Select Publish once for the agent?
Or wait for the save to reach channels?
Decide before I answer.
Select Publish once.
Saving only updates the draft.
One Publish updates every connected channel together.

scenes.title: Why some users see the old version

sentences.text: Now Marta's mystery.
A session is a conversation in progress.
New content only applies when a new session starts.
In most channels, that happens after thirty minutes of inactivity.
Teams keeps conversations open, so the old session can stay alive.
There, the user can type start over to force a new session.
Otherwise, it can take up to an hour.
Your turn.
The fix is published, but Marta's conversation in Teams is still open, and she keeps getting the old answer.
Valeria wants her to see the fix right now.
What should Marta do?
Type start over in the chat?
Publish again just for Teams?
Or reinstall the app in Teams?
Decide before I answer.
Type start over.
It forces a new session, and new sessions get the published content.
Publishing again changes nothing.
So where can users meet the agent?
There is Teams and Microsoft three sixty five.
There is the Demo website, a quick page to try the agent.
And there are others, such as WhatsApp and Facebook.
One family deserves a name: Direct Line channels.
It covers the Demo website, custom websites and mobile apps.
And watch out: some channels require authentication before they work.
Who decides which channels makers may use?
The administrator.
Each channel has its own connector in the data policies.
Teams and Microsoft three sixty five has one.
Direct Line channels has one.
WhatsApp and Facebook have their own.
So if the administrator blocks the WhatsApp and Facebook connectors, makers can no longer use those two channels.
Teams and the website keep working.
Your turn.
Contoso's administrator puts the Direct Line channels connector in the Blocked group of a data policy.
Makers ask which channels they just lost.
Which channels can they no longer use?
Every channel, even Teams?
The Demo website alone?
Or websites and mobile apps?
Decide before I answer.
Websites and mobile apps.
Direct Line covers the Demo website, custom websites and mobile apps.
Teams has its own connector.

scenes.title: Publish and connect in the studio

sentences.text: Here is how it looks in the studio.
Open Nexo and check that your changes are saved.
Select Publish and confirm.
Then go to Channels to see which ones are available.
Pick one, for example Teams or the Demo website, and follow its connection steps.
Check whether it requires authentication.
Finally, open a new conversation in the channel to see your change.
Back at Contoso.
Marta types start over, and Nexo gives her the new returns answer.
Nothing was broken.
Her session had simply started before the fix.
Remember three things.
One Publish updates every channel.
Only a new session sees the change.
And each channel has its own connector in the data policies.
